title: PROMOTION OF TRADITIONAL MARTIAL ARTS ACT
full_text:
PROMOTION OF TRADITIONAL MARTIAL ARTS ACT
Consolidated English translation draft based on Korean source version 279673 (KR:010727)

Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of this Act is to contribute to the enhancement of public health, the improvement of cultural life, and the development of the nation as a cultural state by promoting traditional martial arts possessing cultural value and passing their values on to future generations.

Article 2 (Definitions)
The terms used in this Act shall have the following meanings:
1. "Traditional martial arts" means martial methods, techniques, or systems of combat that originated and became systematized in Korea, or that were introduced from outside Korea and independently formalized and systematized in Korea, that have been handed down over many generations, and that demonstrate the distinctive character of Korean culture.
2. "Traditional martial arts instructor" means a person who teaches traditional martial arts at a school, workplace, local community, or other place.
3. "Traditional martial arts designated for promotion" means a traditional martial arts discipline falling under subparagraph 1, recognized as having traditional, cultural, and sporting value warranting promotion at the national level (including martial arts designated as national intangible heritage under the Act on the Preservation and Promotion of Intangible Heritage), and designated by the Minister of Culture, Sports and Tourism pursuant to Article 6.

Article 3 (Establishment of Basic Plans for Promotion of Traditional Martial Arts, etc.)
(1) The Minister of Culture, Sports and Tourism shall establish and implement a comprehensive basic plan concerning traditional martial arts every five years (hereinafter referred to as the "basic plan") to systematically preserve and promote traditional martial arts.
(2) The basic plan shall include each of the following matters:
1. Basic directions for promoting traditional martial arts;
2. Surveys, research, and related matters for promoting traditional martial arts;
3. Designation of and support for traditional martial arts designated for promotion;
4. Education and training of traditional martial arts instructors;
5. Exchanges and cooperation concerning traditional martial arts, and the holding of competitions;
6. Ways to secure and efficiently use funds necessary for promoting traditional martial arts;
7. Safety, hygiene, and infectious-disease prevention and control at traditional martial arts facilities;
8. Other matters necessary for promoting traditional martial arts, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 4 (Responsibilities of the State and Local Governments)
(1) The State and local governments shall establish and implement various policies for promoting traditional martial arts in accordance with the basic plan.
(2) The State and local governments shall encourage, protect, and foster voluntary traditional martial arts activities by the public and establish an enabling environment, including the provision of necessary facilities, personnel and organizations, and budgetary support.

Article 5 (Survey of the State of Traditional Martial Arts)
(1) The Minister of Culture, Sports and Tourism may conduct surveys of the state of traditional martial arts for use in establishing and implementing policies to promote traditional martial arts.
(2) Where necessary for such surveys, the Minister may request relevant data from the heads of related central administrative agencies, the heads of local governments, the heads of public institutions under Article 4 of the Act on the Management of Public Institutions, or traditional martial arts organizations under Article 8. Those receiving a request shall comply unless they have special reasons not to do so.
(3) Matters necessary for the scope and methods of surveys under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 6 (Designation of Traditional Martial Arts for Promotion)
(1) The Minister of Culture, Sports and Tourism may designate as traditional martial arts for promotion those disciplines which, among traditional martial arts, are recognized as having traditional, cultural, and sporting value warranting national promotion.
(2) Matters necessary for the criteria and procedures for designation of such disciplines shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism.
(3) Upon designating a discipline for promotion, the Minister shall publicly announce the purpose and details of the designation.

Article 7 (Revocation or Withdrawal of Designation)
(1) Where the designation under Article 6 has been obtained by false or other improper means, the Minister of Culture, Sports and Tourism shall revoke the designation.
(2) The Minister may withdraw the designation of a discipline for promotion if any of the following applies:
1. The discipline and the organization concerned cease to exist;
2. The discipline loses its distinctive characteristics;
3. The need to promote the discipline at the national level has substantially diminished.
(3) Before revoking a designation under paragraph (1) or withdrawing it under paragraph (2), the Minister may hear the opinions of relevant traditional martial arts institutions and organizations.
(4) Matters necessary for revocation or withdrawal under paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism.
(5) When a designation is revoked or withdrawn, the Minister shall publicly announce the purpose and details thereof.

Article 8 (Development of Traditional Martial Arts Organizations)
The State and local governments shall develop and support traditional martial arts organizations for the promotion of traditional martial arts; local governments may provide all or part of their operating expenses.

Article 9 (Establishment of the UNESCO International Centre of Martial Arts)
(1) To encourage implementation of the Agreement between the Government of the Republic of Korea and UNESCO regarding the International Centre of Martial Arts for Youth Development and Engagement under the auspices of UNESCO (Category 2), and to preserve and promote traditional martial arts worldwide, the UNESCO International Centre of Martial Arts (hereinafter referred to as the "International Centre of Martial Arts") is hereby established.
(2) The International Centre of Martial Arts shall be a corporation.
(3) The International Centre of Martial Arts shall have officers and such staff as are necessary, as prescribed by its articles of incorporation.
(4) Except as otherwise provided by this Act, the provisions of the Civil Act governing incorporated foundations shall apply mutatis mutandis to the International Centre of Martial Arts.
(5) The State and local governments may, within the limits of their budgets, subsidize expenses necessary for the operation of the International Centre of Martial Arts.

Article 10 (Development of Traditional Martial Arts Instructors, etc.)
(1) The Minister of Culture, Sports and Tourism shall devise necessary measures for developing traditional martial arts instructors and improving their qualifications for the promotion of traditional martial arts.
(2) Matters necessary for the types, grades, qualification requirements, and granting of qualifications for traditional martial arts instructors shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 11 (Qualification Examinations for Traditional Martial Arts Instructors, etc.)
(1) Qualification examinations and training for traditional martial arts instructors shall be conducted by the Minister of Culture, Sports and Tourism: Provided, That where the Minister considers it necessary, a traditional martial arts organization under Article 8, a school under Article 2 of the Higher Education Act, or a sports organization under subparagraph 9 of Article 2 of the National Sports Promotion Act may be designated to conduct such qualification examinations and training.
(2) The head of an institution conducting qualification examinations and training pursuant to the proviso to paragraph (1) may, with the approval of the Minister of Culture, Sports and Tourism, require persons wishing to take such an examination or undergo training to bear part of the expenses necessary therefor.
(3) Matters necessary for qualification examinations and training under paragraph (1), and for the issuance of certificates of qualification, shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism.

Article 12 (Support for Education in Traditional Martial Arts)
The Minister of Culture, Sports and Tourism may support projects prescribed by Presidential Decree, including education and the development of professional personnel, so that the values of traditional martial arts can be passed on to and developed by future generations.

Article 13 (Support for Competitions and International Exchanges)
(1) The Minister of Culture, Sports and Tourism may carry out projects such as holding domestic and international competitions, dispatching traditional martial arts instructors, and undertaking overseas promotion in order to promote traditional martial arts.
(2) In order to efficiently implement projects under paragraph (1), the Minister may entrust relevant institutions or organizations prescribed by Presidential Decree with the projects or have them carry out the projects on the Minister's behalf, and may subsidize all or part of the necessary expenses within budgetary limits.

Article 14 (Delegation and Entrustment of Authority, etc.)
(1) The Minister of Culture, Sports and Tourism may delegate part of the authority under this Act, as prescribed by Presidential Decree, to the Mayor of a Special City or Metropolitan City, a provincial governor, the Mayor of a Special Self-Governing City, the Governor of a Special Self-Governing Province, or the head of a city, county, or autonomous district.
(2) The Minister may entrust part of the affairs relating to the promotion of traditional martial arts under this Act to relevant institutions or organizations, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.

ADDENDA <Act No. 21094, November 11, 2025>

Article 1 (Enforcement Date)
This Act shall enter into force six months after the date of its promulgation.

Article 2 (Amendment to Another Act)
A part of the National Sports Promotion Act is amended as follows:
In Article 2, subparagraph 9 (d), "Article 5" shall be replaced with "Article 8".
